title: perf(canary): adaptive auto-detection and hysteresis rollout guards for performance canaries
author: Asha Mehta
description: Context: ongoing incidents and noisy canary alerts showed that short-lived latency spikes during background KV cache warming and autoscaling events caused canary rollbacks and unnecessary traffic shifts. This PR introduces adaptive auto-detection of throughput/latency regressions and a hysteresis-based rollout guard to reduce flapping while preserving fast rollback on real regressions. Changes include an online sensitivity estimator for canary detectors, per-route KV-aware hysteresis windows, and a policy migration path to opt-in beta. Checklist: - Add adaptive detector and unit tests - Add hysteresis policy and rollout guard wiring - Expose config via perf-canary Helm values and Console feature flag - Backward-compatible defaults and migration notes - Add docs and e2e perf smoke tests Related: ENG-3214, ENG-3228 Motivation and design: the detector now computes an exponential moving variance and auto-tunes its alert threshold based on recent sequence-length and KV cache hit distributions so that short transient warmups do not falsely trigger regressions. Hysteresis is implemented as a stateful comparator with separate engage/disengage thresholds and minimum observation windows to require sustained deviation before initiating traffic rollback. Rollout guards tie into existing canary state machine to prevent immediate rollback unless both throughput and tail-latency regressions exceed adaptive thresholds for the configured window. The implementation is conservative by default and can be tuned per-customer via Helm values or per-route overrides in the Console. Testing and validation: unit tests cover detector edge cases and hysteresis transitions. Perf canary integration tests run in CI with a synthetic workload generator that simulates warmup spikes, KV-cache churn, and genuine regressions. We ran a staged rollout across perf-canary clusters for one week; observed a 78% reduction in false-positive rollbacks on synthetic warmup scenarios and no missed real regressions in the validation set. Migration: defaults are non-breaking; operators can enable the adaptive detector and hysteresis via Helm flag perfCanary.adaptiveHysteresis.enabled=true or via Console feature flag perf_canary.adaptive_hysteresis. Monitoring: adds new metrics perf_canary.detector.sensitivity and perf_canary.hysteresis.state, and dashboard panels to Console. Rollout plan: canary in canary-clusters -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with manual gate at 50%. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3214/perf-canary-adaptive-detection and internal runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/perf-canary-hysteresis

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can you explain how the adaptive threshold reacts to sudden traffic profile shifts? I want to ensure we don't mask genuine regressions during traffic spikes.

Asha Mehta: The estimator uses separate short and long windows; short-window increases sensitivity to rapid changes and long-window prevents overreaction. Hysteresis requires sustained deviation on both throughput and p99 to trigger rollback. Added comment and expanded tests to cover sudden profile changes.
Marcus Lee: Please make sure the new metrics have clear tag dimensions for route/model/version; also add a dashboard panel for hysteresis.state.
Asha Mehta: Added metric labels and a Console dashboard JSON. Also added migration notes to docs and helm values to toggle per-route.
Priya Raman: Verified staged rollout data. Observed reduced flapping in test clusters. Approving pending one small logging cleanup.
Asha Mehta: removed debug logs and addressed nits. Thanks!
release_notes: Adaptive canary detection and hysteresis rollout guards: improves stability of performance canaries by reducing false-positive rollbacks during KV cache warmups and autoscaling. Operators can enable the feature via Helm or Console; conservative defaults are non-breaking.
